questions.prompt: Which expression is most suitable when introducing a visitor to your class teacher?
options: Excuse me, Madam, this is our visitor, Mr. Otieno.
Move aside, this person wants you.
Here is someone; deal with him.
questions.correctAnswer: Excuse me, Madam, this is our visitor, Mr. Otieno.
questions.explanation: A polite introduction uses respectful language, names the person, and gives helpful information.
questions.learningOutcome: Use appropriate polite expressions when introducing people in formal and informal situations.

questions.prompt: During a group discussion, which action shows good turn-taking?
options: Waiting for a speaker to finish before responding
questions.correctAnswer: Waiting for a speaker to finish before responding
questions.explanation: Turn-taking helps speakers listen, respond thoughtfully, and keep a conversation respectful.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply turn-taking rules during conversations and group discussions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence politely interrupts a speaker during a debate practice?
options: May I add a point when you finish?
You are wrong, so sit down.
I will speak whether you like it or not.
questions.correctAnswer: May I add a point when you finish?
questions.explanation: A polite interruption asks for permission and respects the current speaker.
questions.learningOutcome: Use courteous language to enter a conversation without disrupting communication.

questions.prompt: A learner listens to a weather announcement and writes down the day, place, and expected rainfall. Which listening skill is being used?
questions.correctAnswer: Listening for details
questions.explanation: Listening for details focuses on specific information such as time, place, names, and facts.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify specific details from oral texts and announcements.

questions.prompt: Which pair of words best shows the difference between the sounds /p/ and /b/?
questions.correctAnswer: pat and bat
questions.explanation: The words pat and bat differ mainly in the initial /p/ and /b/ sounds.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish selected consonant sounds in spoken English.

questions.prompt: In the noun 'record', where is the stress usually placed?
questions.correctAnswer: On the first syllable: RE-cord
questions.explanation: Many two-syllable nouns such as record place stronger stress on the first syllable.
questions.learningOutcome: Use stress patterns to support clear pronunciation and meaning.

questions.prompt: Which oral narrative opening is common in many Kenyan storytelling traditions?
options: Once upon a time, there lived...
questions.correctAnswer: Once upon a time, there lived...
questions.explanation: Traditional narratives often begin with a familiar opening that signals the start of a story.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common features used when telling oral narratives.

questions.prompt: When collecting an oral narrative from a grandparent, what should a learner do first?
options: Ask for permission and explain the purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Ask for permission and explain the purpose
questions.explanation: Responsible collection of oral narratives begins with respect, consent, and a clear purpose.
questions.learningOutcome: Use respectful strategies when collecting oral narratives from the community.

questions.prompt: Which speaking habit helps an audience follow a class presentation?
options: Speaking clearly at a suitable pace
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking clearly at a suitable pace
questions.explanation: Clear speech and a steady pace make ideas easier for listeners to understand.
questions.learningOutcome: Present information clearly using suitable volume, pace, and posture.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows active listening in a pair discussion?
options: So you are saying that the story teaches honesty.
I did not hear you and I do not care.
I will answer before you explain.
questions.correctAnswer: So you are saying that the story teaches honesty.
questions.explanation: Restating a speaker's idea shows that the listener is following and checking meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate active listening by paraphrasing and responding appropriately.

questions.prompt: Which word contains the long /i:/ sound?
questions.correctAnswer: seat
questions.explanation: The vowel sound in seat is long /i:/, while the other words have the short /i/ sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate short and long vowel sounds in spoken words.

questions.prompt: Which phrase would best close a respectful telephone conversation with a school librarian?
options: Thank you for your help. Goodbye.
I am done, so stop talking.
That is all. Leave me alone.
questions.correctAnswer: Thank you for your help. Goodbye.
questions.explanation: A courteous closing thanks the listener and ends the conversation politely.
questions.learningOutcome: Use polite openings and closings in telephone conversations.

questions.prompt: In a choral verse, why should learners keep the same rhythm?
options: It helps the group sound united and clear
It hides the meaning of the words
It removes the need to practise
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the group sound united and clear
questions.explanation: Shared rhythm supports fluency, expression, and teamwork in a choral performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Perform choral verse using rhythm, clarity, and expression.

questions.prompt: A speaker says, 'I agree with Amina because she gave evidence from the text.' What discussion skill is shown?
options: Supporting a point with a reason
questions.correctAnswer: Supporting a point with a reason
questions.explanation: A strong discussion response links agreement or disagreement to evidence or a clear reason.
questions.learningOutcome: Give relevant reasons when responding to ideas in group discussions.

questions.prompt: Which question would help a learner interview a community elder about oral narratives?
options: What lesson does this story teach young people?
How much money do you have?
Why are old people always wrong?
Can I skip listening and write my own ending?
questions.correctAnswer: What lesson does this story teach young people?
questions.explanation: An effective interview question is respectful and helps gather useful information about the narrative.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask relevant and respectful questions when gathering oral information.

questions.prompt: Which feature makes a speech more persuasive?
options: Relevant examples that support the main point
questions.correctAnswer: Relevant examples that support the main point
questions.explanation: Examples make an argument clearer and help listeners see why the point matters.
questions.learningOutcome: Use relevant examples and reasons to make a spoken point convincing.

questions.prompt: Which action best helps a learner prepare to retell a folktale accurately?
options: Note the setting, main characters, problem, and lesson
Remove all dialogue from the story
questions.correctAnswer: Note the setting, main characters, problem, and lesson
questions.explanation: Retelling is clearer when the speaker understands the key story elements and sequence.
questions.learningOutcome: Retell oral narratives using accurate sequence and key details.

questions.prompt: A learner is asked to listen to instructions for a safety drill. What is the best note-taking approach?
options: Write the steps in the order they are given
Wait until the drill ends and guess
questions.correctAnswer: Write the steps in the order they are given
questions.explanation: Instructions should be recorded in sequence so they can be followed correctly.
questions.learningOutcome: Record and follow oral instructions in the correct order.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why tone matters in spoken communication?
options: Tone can show attitude and affect how a message is received
Tone replaces all words in a sentence
Tone is useful only in written exams
questions.correctAnswer: Tone can show attitude and affect how a message is received
questions.explanation: The way words are spoken can make them sound respectful, rude, serious, or friendly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how tone affects meaning in spoken interactions.

questions.prompt: Which plan best fits a short oral presentation about keeping the school compound clean?
options: State the problem, give two reasons, suggest action, and conclude
Read random sentences from different books
Start with a conclusion and hide the main idea
questions.correctAnswer: State the problem, give two reasons, suggest action, and conclude
questions.explanation: A clear presentation has a focused structure that guides listeners from the issue to a conclusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Organize spoken information into a clear beginning, body, and conclusion.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of this sentence: 'Planting trees near rivers protects soil, keeps water clean, and gives shade'?
options: Planting trees near rivers has several benefits
Shade is the only reason to plant trees
questions.correctAnswer: Planting trees near rivers has several benefits
questions.explanation: The sentence lists several ways trees help river environments, so the main idea is their benefits.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the main idea in short informational texts.

questions.prompt: A story title is 'The Lost Calf'. What is the most reasonable prediction before reading?
options: The story may involve searching for a missing young cow
The story must be about building a road
The story cannot have any characters
The story is only about rainfall measurements
questions.correctAnswer: The story may involve searching for a missing young cow
questions.explanation: A title can suggest likely characters, events, or problems before reading begins.
questions.learningOutcome: Make reasonable predictions from titles and early clues in a text.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The candidate gave a concise speech that ended in five minutes,' what does 'concise' mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Brief and clear
questions.explanation: The clue 'ended in five minutes' suggests that the speech was short and direct.
questions.learningOutcome: Use context clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words.

questions.prompt: Which detail is most important when summarising a story about a girl who solves a water shortage at school?
options: How the girl helped solve the water shortage
The exact colour of every classroom door
The number of clouds in the sky
The brand of every learner's shoes
questions.correctAnswer: How the girl helped solve the water shortage
questions.explanation: A summary keeps the central problem and solution, while leaving out minor details.
questions.learningOutcome: Select key ideas for a concise summary of a narrative text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion rather than a fact?
options: Poetry is the most enjoyable form of writing.
A stanza is a group of lines in a poem.
questions.correctAnswer: Poetry is the most enjoyable form of writing.
questions.explanation: An opinion expresses a personal judgement that others may not share.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish facts from opinions in reading texts.

questions.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to 'assist'?
questions.correctAnswer: Help
questions.explanation: Assist means to help someone do something.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify synonyms to improve vocabulary and comprehension.

questions.prompt: Which word is an antonym of 'generous'?
questions.correctAnswer: Mean
questions.explanation: Generous means willing to give or share, while mean can mean unwilling to give.
questions.learningOutcome: Use antonyms to clarify word meanings in context.

questions.prompt: Which feature is most likely to appear in a poem?
options: A table of exam marks only
questions.correctAnswer: Rhythm and imagery
questions.explanation: Poems often use rhythm, sound patterns, and vivid images to create meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic features of poetry in selected texts.

questions.prompt: In a story, what does the setting tell the reader?
options: The number of pages in a dictionary
questions.correctAnswer: Where and when events happen
questions.explanation: The setting gives the time and place of events in a narrative.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify setting as a key element in narrative texts.

questions.prompt: A character returns a lost wallet instead of keeping the money. Which trait is best shown?
questions.correctAnswer: Honesty
questions.explanation: Returning something that belongs to another person shows honesty and integrity.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer character traits from actions in a narrative.

questions.prompt: Which question helps a reader infer a character's motive?
options: Why did the character act that way?
How many letters are in the title?
What colour is the page margin?
questions.correctAnswer: Why did the character act that way?
questions.explanation: A motive is the reason behind an action, so asking why helps the reader infer it.
questions.learningOutcome: Make inferences about characters using evidence from a text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses imagery most clearly?
options: The orange sunset spread over the hills like warm paint.
questions.correctAnswer: The orange sunset spread over the hills like warm paint.
questions.explanation: Imagery uses descriptive language to help readers picture a scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize imagery and explain how it creates mental pictures.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes intensive reading?
options: Reading carefully to understand details and language use
Reading many books quickly for pleasure only
questions.correctAnswer: Reading carefully to understand details and language use
questions.explanation: Intensive reading is close reading for details, vocabulary, structure, and meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Use intensive reading strategies to understand details in a text.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes extensive reading?
options: Reading longer texts independently for enjoyment and general understanding
Reading one sentence repeatedly for spelling only
Reading a dictionary from back to front
questions.correctAnswer: Reading longer texts independently for enjoyment and general understanding
questions.explanation: Extensive reading builds fluency and confidence through broader independent reading.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of extensive reading in language development.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to find the meaning of a word in a printed dictionary?
options: Use alphabetical order and guide words
Search by the last sound only
questions.correctAnswer: Use alphabetical order and guide words
questions.explanation: Dictionaries arrange words alphabetically, and guide words help locate entries quickly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use dictionary features to find meanings and word information.

questions.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Although the road was muddy, the team arrived on time.' What can be inferred?
options: The journey was difficult but the team managed the time well
The team arrived late because of mud
questions.correctAnswer: The journey was difficult but the team managed the time well
questions.explanation: The word 'although' contrasts the muddy road with the successful arrival on time.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer meaning by using connectives and sentence relationships.

questions.prompt: Which line is an example of personification?
options: The wind whispered through the maize.
questions.correctAnswer: The wind whispered through the maize.
questions.explanation: Personification gives human actions or qualities to non-human things.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple examples of personification in literary texts.

questions.prompt: Which option best states the theme of a story where learners share books with a neighbouring school?
questions.correctAnswer: Generosity strengthens learning communities
questions.explanation: A theme is the central message or insight suggested by a text.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify a theme from events and actions in a narrative.

questions.prompt: Which signpost word shows a cause-and-effect relationship?
questions.correctAnswer: Therefore
questions.explanation: Therefore introduces a result or conclusion caused by earlier information.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize connectives that show relationships between ideas.

questions.prompt: A poem repeats the line 'We shall rise again' after every stanza. What is the likely effect?
options: It proves the poem has no message
It changes the poem into a dictionary entry
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes hope and unity
questions.explanation: Repetition can stress an important idea and make a poem memorable.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how repetition contributes to meaning in poetry.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best summarises this idea: 'Musa wakes early, revises daily, asks questions, and keeps a timetable'?
questions.correctAnswer: Musa uses disciplined study habits.
questions.explanation: The listed actions all support the general idea that Musa is organised in his studies.
questions.learningOutcome: Condense related details into one accurate summary sentence.

questions.prompt: Which feature helps a reader identify dialogue in a story?
options: A page number at the bottom
questions.correctAnswer: Quotation marks around spoken words
questions.explanation: Quotation marks commonly show the exact words spoken by characters.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify dialogue and its punctuation in narrative texts.

questions.prompt: Which option is the best evidence that a speaker in a poem feels lonely?
options: The speaker says, 'No footsteps came to my door all evening.'
The title is printed in bold.
The poet uses a comma in line two.
questions.correctAnswer: The speaker says, 'No footsteps came to my door all evening.'
questions.explanation: Evidence should directly support the interpretation, and this line suggests isolation.
questions.learningOutcome: Select textual evidence to support an interpretation.

questions.prompt: Which reading strategy is most useful before reading a long article about climate change?
options: Preview the title, headings, and pictures
Ignore the title and start at the last word
questions.correctAnswer: Preview the title, headings, and pictures
questions.explanation: Previewing prepares the reader by activating prior knowledge and predicting content.
questions.learningOutcome: Use previewing to prepare for reading informational texts.

questions.prompt: A reader compares two stories and notices both heroes solve problems by cooperating with neighbours. What skill is the reader using?
questions.correctAnswer: Comparing themes across texts
questions.explanation: The reader is identifying a shared message or pattern across two different texts.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare themes and ideas across related literary texts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a count noun correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: The learner borrowed three books.
questions.explanation: Book is a count noun, so it can be used with a number and a plural form.
questions.learningOutcome: Use count and non-count nouns correctly in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word is a collective noun?
questions.correctAnswer: team
questions.explanation: A collective noun names a group of people, animals, or things as one unit.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common, proper, abstract, and collective nouns.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with the correct possessive pronoun.
questions.correctAnswer: This exercise book is mine.
questions.explanation: Mine is a possessive pronoun that can stand alone without a noun after it.
questions.learningOutcome: Use possessive pronouns correctly in spoken and written sentences.

questions.prompt: Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence: 'Amina and Brian said ___ would clean the board'?
questions.correctAnswer: they
questions.explanation: They refers to the plural subject Amina and Brian.
questions.learningOutcome: Select personal pronouns that agree with their nouns.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the simple past tense?
options: The class will visit the museum.
The class is visiting the museum.
questions.correctAnswer: The class visited the museum.
questions.explanation: Visited shows that the action happened in the past.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify and use simple verb tenses accurately.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement.
options: The players has trained every evening.
questions.correctAnswer: The players train every evening.
questions.explanation: The plural subject players takes the base verb train in the simple present tense.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply subject-verb agreement in simple present tense sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb in the sentence 'The goalkeeper moved quickly'?
questions.correctAnswer: quickly
questions.explanation: Quickly describes how the goalkeeper moved, so it is an adverb.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify adverbs that describe how actions are done.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a comparative adjective correctly?
options: This path is safer than the old one.
This path is safest than the old one.
This path is more safer than the old one.
This path is safe than the old one.
questions.correctAnswer: This path is safer than the old one.
questions.explanation: Safer is the correct comparative form of safe when comparing two things.
questions.learningOutcome: Use comparative adjectives to compare two people, places, or things.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a superlative adjective correctly?
options: Of the three routes, this is the shortest.
Of the three routes, this is shorter.
Of the three routes, this is more short.
Of the three routes, this is most shortest.
questions.correctAnswer: Of the three routes, this is the shortest.
questions.explanation: The superlative form shortest is used when comparing more than two routes.
questions.learningOutcome: Use superlative adjectives to compare three or more items.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: Where did you keep the library card?
Where did you keep the library card.
Where did you keep the library card,
Where did you keep the library card
questions.correctAnswer: Where did you keep the library card?
questions.explanation: A direct question should end with a question mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Use question marks correctly in direct questions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a comma correctly in a list?
options: We packed pencils, rulers, books and charts.
We packed pencils rulers books and charts.
We packed, pencils rulers books and charts.
We packed pencils rulers, books and charts.
questions.correctAnswer: We packed pencils, rulers, books and charts.
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a list to make the meaning clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Use commas to separate items in a list.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction best completes the sentence: 'The team practised hard ___ they won the match'?
questions.correctAnswer: so
questions.explanation: So shows the result of practising hard.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conjunctions to show relationships between ideas.

questions.prompt: Choose the preposition that completes the sentence: 'The notice was pinned ___ the board'?
questions.correctAnswer: on
questions.explanation: A notice is pinned on a board because it is attached to its surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Use common prepositions to show position and direction.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly changes 'The learners clean the hall' into the passive voice?
options: The hall is cleaned by the learners.
The learners are cleaned by the hall.
questions.correctAnswer: The hall is cleaned by the learners.
questions.explanation: In the passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
questions.learningOutcome: Transform simple active sentences into passive sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly reports this speech: Mary said, 'I am ready'?
options: Mary said that she was ready.
Mary said that I am ready.
Mary said she is ready yesterday.
Mary said that ready she was.
questions.correctAnswer: Mary said that she was ready.
questions.explanation: Reported speech changes the pronoun and usually shifts the tense back in past reporting.
questions.learningOutcome: Report simple spoken statements using accurate pronouns and tense shifts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly to show possession?
options: The teacher's desk is near the window.
The teachers desk is near the window.
The teacher,s desk is near the window.
The teachers' is desk near the window.
questions.correctAnswer: The teacher's desk is near the window.
questions.explanation: Teacher's shows that the desk belongs to one teacher.
questions.learningOutcome: Use apostrophes to show singular possession.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the correct plural form?
questions.correctAnswer: The children carried the boxes.
questions.explanation: Children is the plural of child, and boxes is the plural of box.
questions.learningOutcome: Form regular and common irregular plural nouns correctly.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the present continuous tense?
options: The learners plant seedlings every term.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners are planting seedlings.
questions.explanation: Are planting shows an action happening now or around the present time.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify and use the present continuous tense in context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the future tense correctly?
options: We shall visit the library tomorrow.
We are visit the library tomorrow.
questions.correctAnswer: We shall visit the library tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Shall visit correctly shows an action that will happen in the future.
questions.learningOutcome: Use future tense forms to describe planned actions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains an adjective?
questions.correctAnswer: The careful driver slowed down.
questions.explanation: Careful describes the noun driver, so it is an adjective.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify adjectives and use them to describe nouns.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an adverb of frequency?
options: The class usually reads after lunch.
The class reads loudly after lunch.
The class reads under a tree.
questions.correctAnswer: The class usually reads after lunch.
questions.explanation: Usually tells how often the class reads, so it is an adverb of frequency.
questions.learningOutcome: Use adverbs of frequency to describe how often actions happen.

questions.prompt: Which option correctly combines the sentences 'It was raining. We continued playing'?
options: Although it was raining, we continued playing.
Because it was raining, we continued playing not.
It was raining but although we continued.
We continued playing because it was not raining.
questions.correctAnswer: Although it was raining, we continued playing.
questions.explanation: Although introduces a contrast between the rain and the action that continued.
questions.learningOutcome: Join related ideas using subordinating conjunctions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the article 'an' correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: She carried an umbrella.
questions.explanation: An is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, such as umbrella.
questions.learningOutcome: Use a, an, and the appropriately in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically complete?
questions.correctAnswer: The learners prepared a poster.
questions.explanation: A complete sentence has a subject and a predicate that express a full thought.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify complete sentences and sentence fragments.

questions.prompt: Which sentence avoids a double negative?
options: I have not seen no notice.
questions.correctAnswer: I have seen the notice.
questions.explanation: Standard English avoids using two negatives to express one negative idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize and correct common non-standard sentence forms.

questions.prompt: Which word correctly completes the sentence: 'Each of the boys ___ a dictionary'?
questions.correctAnswer: has
questions.explanation: Each is singular, so it takes the singular verb has.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply subject-verb agreement with indefinite pronouns and singular expressions.

questions.prompt: Which option correctly punctuates direct speech?
options: Please close the door, said Njeri.
Please close the door" said Njeri.
questions.correctAnswer: "Please close the door," said Njeri.
questions.explanation: Direct speech is placed in quotation marks, and the comma belongs inside the closing quotation mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Punctuate direct speech using quotation marks and reporting clauses.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the clearest pronoun reference?
options: After Asha met Wanjiku, Asha shared her notes.
After Asha met Wanjiku, she shared her notes.
Asha and Wanjiku met because she had notes.
When she met her, she gave them to her.
questions.correctAnswer: After Asha met Wanjiku, Asha shared her notes.
questions.explanation: Repeating Asha makes it clear who shared the notes and avoids confusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise sentences to make pronoun references clear.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses parallel structure correctly?
options: The club teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
The club teaches reading, writing, and how to speak.
The club teaches to read, writing, and speech.
The club teaches read, wrote, and speaking.
questions.correctAnswer: The club teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
questions.explanation: Parallel structure uses the same grammatical pattern for items in a list.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise lists and paired ideas for parallel grammatical structure.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines ideas without changing meaning: 'The river rose. The bridge remained safe. The rain was heavy'?
options: Although the rain was heavy and the river rose, the bridge remained safe.
The bridge was heavy because the river rained safely.
The river remained heavy although the bridge rained.
The rain was safe because the bridge rose.
questions.correctAnswer: Although the rain was heavy and the river rose, the bridge remained safe.
questions.explanation: The combined sentence preserves the contrast between difficult conditions and the safe bridge.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine related clauses into coherent complex sentences.

questions.prompt: Which topic sentence best begins a paragraph about saving water at school?
options: Learners can save water at school in several practical ways.
Water is a word with five letters.
questions.correctAnswer: Learners can save water at school in several practical ways.
questions.explanation: A topic sentence introduces the main idea that the paragraph will explain.
questions.learningOutcome: Write focused topic sentences for well-developed paragraphs.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would best support the topic 'Trees improve the school environment'?
options: They provide shade and reduce dust in the compound.
The clock is on the wall.
questions.correctAnswer: They provide shade and reduce dust in the compound.
questions.explanation: A supporting sentence should add a relevant reason, example, or detail about the topic.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop paragraphs using relevant supporting details.

questions.prompt: Which closing sentence best ends a paragraph about teamwork?
options: For these reasons, teamwork helps learners achieve more together.
There are clouds in the sky.
questions.correctAnswer: For these reasons, teamwork helps learners achieve more together.
questions.explanation: A closing sentence should link back to the paragraph's main idea and give it a clear finish.
questions.learningOutcome: Write concluding sentences that complete a paragraph logically.

questions.prompt: Which feature is most important in a school notice?
options: Clear purpose, date, time, venue, and contact person
Long jokes unrelated to the event
questions.correctAnswer: Clear purpose, date, time, venue, and contact person
questions.explanation: A notice should quickly tell readers what is happening, when, where, and who is involved.
questions.learningOutcome: Write notices using essential details and clear layout.

questions.prompt: Which heading is most suitable for a poster encouraging learners to keep classrooms clean?
questions.correctAnswer: Keep Our Classrooms Clean
questions.explanation: A poster heading should be short, direct, and linked to the intended message.
questions.learningOutcome: Design poster headings that communicate a clear message.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is most appropriate for a formal letter to the head teacher?
options: I kindly request permission to use the hall for debate practice.
The hall is ours whether you agree or not.
questions.correctAnswer: I kindly request permission to use the hall for debate practice.
questions.explanation: Formal letters require respectful language and a clear request.
questions.learningOutcome: Use polite and formal language when writing official requests.

questions.prompt: Which part of an informal letter usually comes after the writer's address and date?
questions.correctAnswer: Greeting
questions.explanation: An informal letter normally begins with the writer's address and date, followed by a greeting.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify parts of an informal letter and arrange them correctly.

questions.prompt: Which sentence improves coherence in a paragraph about planting trees?
options: In addition, trees attract birds and make the compound beautiful.
The answer is on page six.
questions.correctAnswer: In addition, trees attract birds and make the compound beautiful.
questions.explanation: The phrase in addition links a new related point to the previous idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Use linking words to connect ideas logically in paragraphs.

questions.prompt: Which order best fits a narrative composition?
questions.correctAnswer: Beginning, rising action, climax, ending
questions.explanation: A narrative usually develops events from an opening through a problem or climax to an ending.
questions.learningOutcome: Organize narrative writing using a logical sequence of events.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses dialogue correctly in a story?
options: Let us hurry, said Kamau without quotes.
Let us hurry" said Kamau without comma.
questions.correctAnswer: "Let us hurry," said Kamau.
questions.explanation: Dialogue should use quotation marks and suitable punctuation around the spoken words.
questions.learningOutcome: Write dialogue using quotation marks and reporting clauses correctly.

questions.prompt: Which detail would make a descriptive paragraph about a market more vivid?
options: The smell of ripe mangoes filled the busy stalls.
questions.correctAnswer: The smell of ripe mangoes filled the busy stalls.
questions.explanation: Vivid description uses sensory details to help readers imagine the scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Use sensory details to create vivid descriptions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence should be removed from a paragraph about safe road crossing?
options: Use a zebra crossing where available.
questions.correctAnswer: My favourite fruit is pineapple.
questions.explanation: A paragraph should keep only details that support its main idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise paragraphs by removing irrelevant sentences.

questions.prompt: Which plan would best help a learner write a summary of a two-page passage?
options: Identify the main points, remove examples, and write in fewer words
Add new stories not in the passage
Keep only the last word of each paragraph
questions.correctAnswer: Identify the main points, remove examples, and write in fewer words
questions.explanation: A good summary keeps essential ideas and leaves out unnecessary details.
questions.learningOutcome: Summarize texts by selecting main points and omitting minor details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is most suitable for the conclusion of an article about reading culture?
options: In conclusion, regular reading helps learners gain knowledge and confidence.
The chair was beside the window.
I forgot my lunch box yesterday.
There are seven days in a week.
questions.correctAnswer: In conclusion, regular reading helps learners gain knowledge and confidence.
questions.explanation: A conclusion should restate the main idea and leave the reader with a final thought.
questions.learningOutcome: Write effective conclusions for short articles and compositions.

questions.prompt: Which revision makes this sentence clearer: 'They did it there after that'?
options: The scouts planted seedlings near the gate after assembly.
questions.correctAnswer: The scouts planted seedlings near the gate after assembly.
questions.explanation: Clear writing names the people, action, place, and time instead of using vague words.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise vague sentences by adding precise nouns, verbs, and details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an example to develop a paragraph about honesty?
options: For example, a learner can return extra change given at the shop.
questions.correctAnswer: For example, a learner can return extra change given at the shop.
questions.explanation: An example gives a specific case that explains or supports the main idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Use examples and incidents to develop paragraph ideas.

questions.prompt: Which incident best supports a paragraph about courage?
options: A learner reports bullying even though friends tell him to keep quiet.
A learner counts desks in class.
A learner reads the timetable silently.
questions.correctAnswer: A learner reports bullying even though friends tell him to keep quiet.
questions.explanation: An incident about taking a difficult but right action supports the idea of courage.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose relevant incidents to support a paragraph's main idea.

questions.prompt: Which format detail belongs in a notice for a club meeting?
options: The price of a novel unrelated to the club
The answer key for a test
questions.correctAnswer: The meeting date and venue
questions.explanation: A notice must give practical details so readers know when and where to attend.
questions.learningOutcome: Include essential format details when writing notices.

questions.prompt: Which slogan is most effective for a poster about protecting school books?
options: Cover it, carry it carefully, and keep it dry.
A very long paragraph with no clear action.
questions.correctAnswer: Cover it, carry it carefully, and keep it dry.
questions.explanation: An effective slogan is brief, memorable, and tells readers what action to take.
questions.learningOutcome: Create short and persuasive poster messages for current issues.

questions.prompt: Which opening best fits an email to a classmate about a group project?
options: Hi Neema, I hope you are well.
To the County Director of Education,
questions.correctAnswer: Hi Neema, I hope you are well.
questions.explanation: An email to a classmate may use a friendly but respectful informal greeting.
questions.learningOutcome: Use suitable greetings and tone in informal digital communication.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best shows formal tone in a report about a school clean-up?
options: The activity began at 8:00 a.m. and involved all Grade 7 learners.
It was, like, a really big thing and stuff.
We just did it and it was cool.
questions.correctAnswer: The activity began at 8:00 a.m. and involved all Grade 7 learners.
questions.explanation: Formal reports use precise, objective language and avoid slang.
questions.learningOutcome: Use formal and objective language in short reports.

questions.prompt: Which checklist best supports editing a composition before submission?
options: Check spelling, punctuation, paragraph unity, and sentence clarity
Check only the colour of the cover
Count the number of desks nearby
Read only the title and stop
questions.correctAnswer: Check spelling, punctuation, paragraph unity, and sentence clarity
questions.explanation: Editing improves correctness and clarity before a final piece of writing is submitted.
questions.learningOutcome: Edit written work for spelling, punctuation, unity, and clarity.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to preserve collected oral narratives in a class anthology. Which writing task is most useful?
options: Arrange the narratives by title, source, community, and lesson
Delete all names and lessons without explanation
Mix every story into one sentence
Keep only pictures and remove the words
questions.correctAnswer: Arrange the narratives by title, source, community, and lesson
questions.explanation: An anthology is easier to read and preserve when entries are organized with useful details.
questions.learningOutcome: Organize collected oral narratives for preservation and sharing.

questions.prompt: Which revision best improves the sentence 'The event was nice' for a descriptive composition?
options: The music, bright decorations, and cheerful speeches made the event memorable.
It was nice because nice things are nice.
questions.correctAnswer: The music, bright decorations, and cheerful speeches made the event memorable.
questions.explanation: Specific details make writing clearer and more interesting than general words such as nice.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise general words into precise and descriptive language.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports writing a balanced paragraph on whether learners should join clubs?
options: State a view, give reasons, include an example, and end with a clear conclusion
Write only the conclusion and no reasons
List club names without explaining anything
Copy another learner's paragraph word for word
questions.correctAnswer: State a view, give reasons, include an example, and end with a clear conclusion
questions.explanation: A balanced paragraph develops a clear view with reasons, evidence, and a logical ending.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan and write coherent opinion paragraphs with reasons and examples.
